preamble: Click-type merger: the palatal click [ǂ] is replaced by the dental click [ǀ]. In Yeyi (Bantu), the Namibian variety has merged Botswana Yeyi's palatal and dental clicks into dental (Sands & Gunnink 2019). The Tshwa (East Kalahari Khoe) article on Wikipedia reports that the dozen words beginning with ǂ are pronounced with ǀ by younger speakers, but gives no forms. In Fwe (Bantu), click type is not contrastive and the same word can have ǀ, ǂ or ǁ, with dental the most common; that is synchronic free variation, not a historical change, and it is marked as allophony below. Fwe also borrows Ju palatal-click words with a dental click. The Yeyi and Fwe-variation parts rest on one form each and the Ju loans on two; together there are three independent cases.
